title: LLMs for Agentic AI
oneLiner: An agent is a language model that works in a loop: it plans, uses tools, looks at the results and decides what to do next, until the job is done, with guardrails so it stays safe.

what.html:
A chatbot answers once. An agent keeps going: it thinks about the goal, calls a tool (search, calculator, database, code), reads the result, updates its memory, and plans the next step. Several agents can also work as a team. Agents can query databases (text-to-SQL), search documents in several hops (agentic RAG), and need safeguards because they can take real actions.

Everyday versionA capable assistant handed a goal ("find our best-selling city and email the team") who looks things up, runs the numbers, drafts the email and checks with you before sending, rather than just answering a single question.

why.html:
• Agents handle multi-step jobs: research, analysis, coding.
  • They are where LLMs start acting in the real world.
  • New abilities bring new risks that need limits and approvals.

how.title: How much autonomy?
how.html: From one call, to fixed workflows, to routers, to agents choosing their own steps, to teams of agents. Use the simplest that works.

how.title: What an agent is made of
how.html: A model plus perception (what it sees), memory (short and long term), planning (breaking down the goal) and tools (ways to act).

how.title: Think, act, observe, repeat
how.html: "Double the population of France": search → about 68 million; calculate 68 × 2 → 136; answer. A step limit stops endless loops.

how.title: Teams of agents
how.html: A manager agent splits the work among a researcher, a writer and a checker. Helpful for big jobs, but costs and coordination grow.

how.title: Agents that query data
how.html: The agent writes a database query, the system checks it's read-only and runs it: Delhi has the most revenue (350). A "delete" request is blocked.

how.title: Search in several hops
how.html: "Who founded the company that makes the Model Q phone?" First find the company, then search for its founder.

how.title: Keep agents safe
how.html: Limits on steps and spending, checked tool inputs, sandboxes, and asking a human before risky actions like payments or emails.

demo.html: Sort each description into memory, planning, tools or safeguards.

example.html:
Small errors add up. If each step works 97% of the time, a 10-step task succeeds only 0.97¹⁰ ≈ 74% of the time. That's why agents check intermediate results and keep tasks short.

Supplementary For well-understood processes, a fixed workflow is often cheaper and more reliable than a free-roaming agent.

misunderstandings: They act in loops with tools.
Tool results can be trusted as instructions.
A smart enough agent needs no limits.
takeaways: Agent = LLM in a loop with tools, memory and planning.
Data agents write SQL/code; validate read-only.
Agentic RAG for multi-hop; safeguards for loops and risky actions.
thirty: Agents are LLMs that choose actions in a loop toward a goal: perceive, reason, act via tools, observe, update memory. Autonomy ranges from single calls to workflows, routers, agent loops and multi-agent systems; use the simplest that works. Architecture: perception, memory (short-term context, long-term stores), planning (decomposition, re-planning) and tools (function calls). The ReAct loop drives most agents (search 68M → calculate 136M → finish, with step limits). Multi-agent patterns: orchestrator–workers, critics, debate, hand-offs; costs and error cascades grow. Data agents generate SQL or pandas code, validated (read-only) and executed (Delhi 350; DELETE blocked). Agentic RAG decides when/what to retrieve and iterates for multi-hop questions. Safeguards: step/budget limits, loop detection, argument validation, sandboxes, least privilege, human approval for risky actions, untrusted tool outputs, logging and evaluation; per-step errors compound (0.97¹⁰ ≈ 0.74).
